entries.task_description: Unified and refactored the bottom padding of all customer-facing views. Replaced hardcoded paddings (like pb-24, pb-32, pb-44) and pb-safe-home with a dynamic pb-customer class driven by a CSS variable --customer-pb. Calculated the variable as calc(64px + safe-area + 16px) on mobile and calc(24px + 64px + 16px) on desktop to match the exact height and offsets of the floating BottomNav. This eliminates the excessive blank/white space at the end of the pages when scrolled to the bottom.
entries.lessons_learned: To prevent excessive blank spaces at the end of scrolling views that sit under fixed bottom nav bars, define a single dynamic CSS variable representing the nav bar height + offsets + safe-area + a unified margin (e.g. 16px). Use this variable across all outer page containers to ensure consistency and precise scroll anchoring on both mobile and desktop viewports.

entries.task_description: Fixed layout bug where the Admin Panel bottom navigation bar was hidden/missing on mobile browsers (Chrome/Safari). The layout used a visual viewport height check 'viewport.height < window.innerHeight * 0.85' to hide the bar when the virtual keyboard was open. However, on mobile browsers with address bars and navigation bars shown, the visual viewport was always smaller than 85% of layout viewport, causing the bottom bar to be permanently hidden. Resolved this by refactoring handleResize in AdminLayout.tsx to check if a text input/textarea is focused before declaring the keyboard active.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing keyboard hiding utilities for sticky/fixed elements using window.visualViewport, avoid comparing viewport.height directly to innerHeight with a small static threshold, as standard mobile browser Chrome (URL bars/tabs/navbars) can easily reduce the height by more than 15%. Instead, check if the active element is a text-focused input or textarea to verify intent to open the keyboard.

entries.task_description: Refactored the Home screen featured promotions area (Super Descontos) inside PremiumOffers.tsx. Replaced the static, key-based remounting single-card transition with a high-fluidity swipeable carousel powered by embla-carousel-react. Implemented loop cycle, touch swipe/drag physics, and custom transition duration. Added custom layout adjustments (negative margin and padding offsets) on the Embla viewport to allow card scale hover transformations and outer shadows to render without boundary clipping. Synchronized indicators and autoplay timer cleanly with Embla's API events.
entries.errors_encountered: ESLint warning for unused 'idx' variable in map callback, resolved by removing unused parameter.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing custom carousels inside scrollable wrappers using Embla or similar libraries, ensure that the viewport wrapper accounts for hover scaling and absolute shadow overlays of slides by applying matching vertical padding and negative margin offsets. This prevents container clipping issues during interactions.

entries.task_description: Optimized the Admin Panel dirty checking efficiency and user exit protection. Refactored the form dirty checking inside AdminProductFormView.tsx to use a shallowCompare helper function isProductFormDirty, removing costly JSON.stringify deep serialization overhead on every keystroke/render cycle. Implemented window-level beforeunload navigation blockers inside App.tsx driven by the global isAdminDirty state to prevent data loss on page reload or tab close. Added high-fidelity server connection latency diagnostics checking RTT against Supabase API in useOnlineStatus.ts, displaying dynamic status indicators and tooltips inside AdminLayout.tsx header and sidebar.
entries.lessons_learned: Centralizing beforeunload listeners in layout wrappers or main application controllers driven by a single state variable (like isAdminDirty) reduces hook duplication and cleanly protects all sub-views. Also, replacing JSON.stringify comparison arrays with field-specific shallowCompare checks completely eliminates garbage collection pressure and CPU lag on large form updates.

entries.task_description: Optimized the Admin Panel UX and loading transitions. Installed a premium animated NProgress-style route progress bar using Framer Motion in App.tsx. Added a glowing green/red connection status indicator (online/offline) with ping animation inside AdminLayout.tsx sidebar and mobile header. Integrated onMouseEnter/onTouchStart prefetch triggers to dynamically warm lazy-loaded product and user details chunks when hovering list cards. Stabilized card heights for detailed/compact products and orders to match loading skeletons exactly, eliminating Cumulative Layout Shifts (CLS). Validated via typecheck and eslint checks.
entries.lessons_learned: Setting matching fixed/min-height properties on card containers relative to their skeleton components completely prevents layout shifting (CLS) on lazy list loads. Integrating micro-transitions (like pulsing glow connection pills and NProgress style loaders) greatly elevates the application's perceived speed and visual polish.

entries.task_description: Optimized the admin panel's visual fluidity, transition smoothness, hook execution order, and offline resilience. First, refactored useOnlineStatus.ts with a locking check and a 1.5s verification retry to filter temporary network blips. Second, systematically grouped all hook declarations (states, refs, callbacks, effects) at the top of AdminQAView.tsx, and simplified realtime subscription callbacks. Third, adjusted AdminViewLoadingFallback in App.tsx to dynamically render page titles using the proper view transition styles, preventing layout shifts during lazy-route loading. Fourth, optimized PhoneSimulator.tsx to sanitize product image lists by filtering out empty strings and handling fallback image placeholders.
entries.lessons_learned: To maintain seamless page transitions with the View Transitions API, skeletal load placeholders should render the text elements of titles using matching styles and transition names instead of blank grey block shimmers. Additionally, grouping React hooks strictly by category (states, refs, callbacks, effects) at the component root prevents HMR hook order mismatch warnings.

entries.task_description: Resolved a race condition in the password recovery flow and provided a premium HTML email template for the user. When users clicked the recovery link, the session was loaded faster than the auth state listener could register isPasswordRecovery=true, causing the app to redirect them to the profile view as a normal login. Solved this by initializing isPasswordRecovery directly from the URL query params/hash fragment on initial load, and cleaning up the URL parameter afterwards. Also designed a gorgeous responsive HTML email template for password reset to replace the default plain Supabase emails.
entries.lessons_learned: When handling redirects that automatically sign in users (like Supabase recovery links), ensure the state that prevents redirection away from the AuthView (e.g. isPasswordRecovery) is initialized synchronously from the URL on mount. In addition, providing clean visual assets like custom HTML email templates completes the design lifecycle for the user.

entries.task_description: Optimized the fluidity, visual stability, and page transitions of the admin panel. First, fixed layout unmounting during lazy load transitions by placing a nested React.Suspense boundary inside the AdminLayout around the sub-views content slot. Second, added all 13 admin sub-routes to usePrefetchOnHover's mapping and attached onMouseEnter/onTouchStart events on bottom/header nav items to start speculatively prefetching module chunks. Third, removed a heavy cyclic state dependency in the image metadata loading useEffect in AdminProductFormView using a useRef of already evaluated URLs. Fourth, deferred heavy Recharts SVG rendering by 180ms during mount using useDeferredRender to avoid frame drops during view transitions.
entries.lessons_learned: When using lazy-loaded routes and a persistent visual layout, always wrap the lazy inner view slot in a nested React.Suspense boundary to avoid unmounting and recreating the layout (header/footer/navs) when views suspend. Additionally, defer CPU-heavy SVG charting (like Recharts) during route transitions using useDeferredRender to maintain 60 FPS transitions.

entries.task_description: Implemented Tabs Keep-Alive pattern for the 5 main admin views in App.tsx by rendering them in parallel and toggling visibility with CSS display: none. Fixed layout wrapper recreation inside AdminLayout by assigning a stable reconciliation key ('admin-main-tabs') for main tabs. Added a passive real-time scroll recording listener inside AdminLayout.tsx to preserve native scroll offsets on hidden layout elements, bypassing clamp/reset issues. Refactored the loading checks in AdminProductsView.tsx to use loading && products.length === 0, preventing skeleton flash during background syncing/refreshing.
entries.lessons_learned: Keeping tab panels mounted in the DOM using class-based toggle (block/hidden) maintains React local states, search inputs, and page indices intact across tab changes. Capturing scrollTop in real-time scroll listeners avoids offset clamps when nodes are hidden. Stale-while-revalidate loading checks are critical to prevent flashing UI loaders on dynamic updates.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel transitions, product variant data integrity, and offline/unstable network resilience. First, wrapped secondary views in AnimatePresence and motion.div inside renderAdminContent in App.tsx for smooth slide/fade animations. Second, implemented upsertVariants in useProducts hook to batch upsert all product variants in a single Supabase call, and refactored AdminProductFormView's handleSubmit to use this batch call instead of a sequential JS loop (preventing duplicate variant insertions on network glitches). Third, added a dynamic connection online/offline state, banner, and button disabled triggers to AdminLayout.tsx and AdminProductFormView.tsx to protect database writes.
entries.lessons_learned: Batching database operations using Supabase upsert avoids inconsistent states and variant duplication issues during client-side network interruptions. Additionally, combining global layout state (online/offline banners) with form button disabled states provides clear visual feedback and prevents broken API requests.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel performance, transition smoothness, scroll restoration stability, and consolidated real-time order subscriptions. Passed an optional onRealtimeEvent callback to useOrders.ts and managed a single channel subscription instead of duplicate manual ones in AdminOrdersView.tsx, resolving duplicate toast notices and saving WebSocket connection limits. Disabled Framer Motion transition durations when View Transitions API is supported to let browser compositor handle transitions without lag. Refactored AdminLayout scroll events to use currentViewRef and deterministic requestAnimationFrame lock to prevent zero-value clamp overwrites.
entries.lessons_learned: Consolidating hooks' auto-subscriptions with views callbacks reduces WebSocket connections and solves duplicate alerts. When View Transitions API is supported, setting Framer Motion durations to 0 prevents visual lag. Finally, scroll restoration locks are best synchronized with browser requestAnimationFrame cycles rather than fixed timeouts.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel fluidity, smoothness, and error resilience. First, added robust try-catch blocks during DataVault IndexedDB initialization in StoreContext.tsx to clean local cache stores on failure, avoiding white-screen hangs. Second, intercepted browser popstate in App.tsx syncWithUrl to prevent accidental exits from sub-admin views (like product forms or details) to customer views, routing back to main admin listings instead. Third, implemented regex sanitization for currency and number values and uppercase conversion for SKUs in AdminProductFormView.tsx. Fourth, added content-visibility: auto classes to AdminProductsView.tsx product cards to optimize layout passes.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing offline caching (IndexedDB/DataVault), error bounds must actively recover from corrupted caches by clearing stores to prevent application hangs. When routing with URL sync and browser history, intercepting back navigation on sub-modules ensures users don't exit administrative portals unexpectedly. Applying CSS content-visibility: auto on large lists significantly improves DOM performance.

entries.task_description: Optimized the admin panel's Keep-Alive persistence by resolving a critical wrapper key recreation bug in AdminLayout.tsx. In addition, improved inactive TabWrapper accessibility and performance in App.tsx by condition-setting visibility and pointer-events. Finally, verified code against strict compilation checks (typecheck and lint) and ran manual browser diagnostics to ensure the search terms and pagination state persist on back navigation.
entries.lessons_learned: When using parallel rendered screens hidden via CSS, ensure no parent container changes its key dynamically, as key shifts trigger complete component unmounts and clear react state/scroll position. Additionally, disabling pointer-events and setting visibility to hidden on hidden tabs prevents keyboard focus jumps and accidental interactions.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel navigation structure by implementing a dynamic contextual back button in AdminLayout.tsx header. When the user visits any sub-view (like product forms, coupons, banners, reviews, qa, or push), the top-left button dynamically updates from 'Perfil' to 'Voltar' and routes directly to the correct parent admin view, resolving confusing navigation paths on mobile and desktop layout configurations. Verified the updates with static typechecks and local production builds.
entries.lessons_learned: Contextual navigation headers improve mobile UX considerably. Standardizing sub-route parent maps in layout structures makes back actions predictable without adding state complexity to individual views.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel state synchronization and fixed background fetching bugs. Guarded the selectedOrderId hook in AdminOrdersView.tsx with the active prop check. When users loaded the orders page and subsequently navigated to edit a product, the background-mounted AdminOrdersView would receive the product's UUID via the shared selectedProductId state and attempt to fetch it as an order ID, triggering console errors and a toast warning. Guarding this with the active prop completely resolved the issue without losing Keep-Alive persistence.
entries.lessons_learned: When keeping tab views mounted in the background (Keep-Alive), any effects that synchronize with shared global state variables (like selection IDs) must check whether their view is currently active. Otherwise, they will intercept IDs meant for other views and trigger failed API/database calls.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel resource utilization, banner reordering stability, and unified network recovery. First, prevented KPI Carousel autoplay background CPU usage in AdminCustomersView, AdminQAView, and AdminBannersView by passing the active prop to pause Embla autoplay and reinitialization on hidden tabs. Second, resolved banner reordering bugs by implementing order normalization during fetch and swap checks inside useBanners.ts, sorting by order/id and updating Supabase to remove order collisions. Third, added automatic background list updates when returning online for banners, coupons, reviews, and QA views.
entries.errors_encountered: React Hook useCallback was missing isAdmin dependency in useBanners.ts; resolved by adding isAdmin to the dependency list.
entries.lessons_learned: Background tabs in keep-alive structures continue running autoplay loops and CSS triggers unless explicitly paused using an active state prop. Passive order normalization in the client prior to DB swaps prevents lockups when users delete/restore items out of order.

entries.task_description: Optimized admin panel fluidity, smoothness, and API efficiency by resolving double-fetch loops on view mounts. In AdminReviewsView, AdminQAView, AdminProductsView, and AdminOrdersView, the page-loading useEffect depended directly on the length of the data array. This caused a second background fetch immediately after the first one succeeded (since the array length changed from 0 to N). Solved by tracking the array length in a synced useRef, removing the array length from the hook's dependencies, and using the ref to calculate the shouldBeSilent flag.
entries.lessons_learned: When loading lists asynchronously, adding list.length to the loading useEffect dependencies can trigger a duplicate immediate load request once the first request resolves and updates the list length. Using a synced useRef of the list length avoids this dependency and prevents redundant network calls.

entries.task_description: Optimized the typing responsiveness and input fluidity in the admin panel by implementing a real debounce mechanism in the LocalBufferedInput and LocalBufferedTextarea components. Previously, these components accepted a delay prop but ignored it, executing the parent update immediately on every keystroke. This caused heavy sessional re-renders of the large 2,600+ lines AdminProductFormView component on every character typed, leading to significant input lag. Solved this by setting a setTimeout debounce (defaulting to 200ms) inside the inputs, and flushing the value immediately on blur to prevent data loss. Verified with full typescript and eslint checks.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing buffered or deferred inputs, always use a proper debounce mechanism to avoid updating large parent component states on every single keystroke. Sychronizing sychronously on blur is a crucial safety net to ensure that form submissions always have the latest user input.

entries.task_description: Optimized the admin layout rendering efficiency and performance. By changing useOrders(true, true) to useOrders(false, true) in AdminLayout.tsx, we eliminated the layout-level active real-time WebSockets subscription and initial fetch of orders. Since AdminLayout doesn't render order lists directly, disabling active loading avoids sessional re-renders of the sidebar, header, and entire navigation wrapper during order updates and page navigations, significantly improving FPS.
entries.lessons_learned: Avoid invoking hooks with active data loading or subscriptions (like WebSockets/real-time) in high-level layout wrappers when the wrapper only needs utility functions (e.g., loadOrders for hover prefetch). Setting enabled: false avoids layout-level updates and avoids massive tree-wide re-renders.

entries.task_description: Optimized the Admin Panel offline resilience and user interaction fluidity. Implemented offline status update queueing (orders_offline_updates_queue) inside useOrders.ts's updateOrderStatus. When offline, order status changes are cached in localStorage and synced automatically once connection is reestablished, mirroring the products sync pattern. Removed offline status modification blockers in AdminOrdersView.tsx to utilize this new queue. Integrated native haptic vibrations (light, medium, success, error) to provide tactile feedback during product toggling, deleting, replicating, and when settings switches are clicked, elevating the tactile experience of the PWA dashboard. Verified with full clean typecheck and eslint validations.
entries.lessons_learned: Enabling offline queues for status changes prevents client-side operation locks and matches the resilience of offline-first product editing. Additionally, adding physical haptic responses to critical administrative actions (toggles, deletions, duplications) completes the PWA design loop for touch interfaces.

entries.task_description: Optimized the fluidity and screen transitions of the admin panel by implementing preloaded lazy routes and synchronous rendering. Created a custom lazyWithPreload utility and PreloadedOrLazy component wrapper to pre-resolve dynamic component imports. Refactored App.tsx to replace standard React.lazy imports with lazyWithPreload, concurrently preloading admin views inside handleNavigate before triggering browser view transitions. Configured a dynamic useEffect to force document-level dark theme during admin views to align background colors. Modified index.css to force background-color: #09090b on html.dark::view-transition to prevent white canvas bleed-through during transitions. Verified with production bundle compilation.
entries.errors_encountered: TypeScript compilation issue: verbatimModuleSyntax required type-only import for ComponentType in lazyWithPreload.ts; resolved by splitting component imports. JSX file extension error: JSX syntax inside lazyWithPreload.ts was disallowed; resolved by converting TSX tags to raw React.createElement calls to keep it as a pure TS file.
entries.lessons_learned: To get perfectly smooth page transitions using View Transitions API without layout snaps or fallback flashes, lazy-loaded components should be preloaded and rendered synchronously during the state update. Additionally, styling the ::view-transition root background color to match the dark theme prevents white bleed-through during canvas animation calculations, and using React.createElement inside utility files avoids TSX file extension validation conflicts.

entries.task_description: Optimized database stability and implemented full real-time synchronization across all tabs (guests and authenticated). Added 8 missing monitored tables (produtos, categorias, banners, store_config, coupons, product_variants, questions, answers) to the supabase_realtime publication via SQL migration. Refactored RealtimeSyncEngine.ts and NotificationContext.tsx using useLeaderElection and BroadcastChannel to ensure only one active Leader Tab opens WebSockets to Supabase, broadcasting updates locally to secondary tabs. Integrated engine startup for guest and logged-in users inside StoreContext.tsx.
entries.lessons_learned: To scale Supabase Realtime in multi-tab PWA applications without hitches or database connection drops, delegate WebSocket connections to a single Leader Tab via coordinate-locks (BroadcastChannel + localStorage) and propagate PostgreSQL change payloads locally to secondary tabs. This guarantees real-time responsiveness while protecting connection limits.

entries.task_description: Enabled and optimized real-time synchronization for Customer Q&A and Reviews across customer-facing ProductView pages and Admin Panel dashboard lists. Added reviews table to the supabase_realtime publication via SQL migration. Upgraded subscribeToQuestions and created subscribeToReviews hooks to support cross-tab coordination using useLeaderElection and BroadcastChannels (ikcous_questions_sync, ikcous_reviews_sync), ensuring only the leader tab holds active websocket connections to Supabase. Fixed typescript implicit any errors on channel subscription parameters.
entries.errors_encountered: TypeScript compilation issue: parameter 'status' and 'err' implicitly had any types inside channel.subscribe callbacks; resolved by adding explicit type annotations.
entries.lessons_learned: For interactive sessional sections like Q&A and Reviews, scoping real-time subscriptions by productId on the Leader Tab and broadcasting reload signals to secondary tabs reduces Supabase WebSocket load while maintaining instant visual updates during customer-admin dialogs. Keep TypeScript strict rules in mind and always explicitly type parameters in websocket callback events.

entries.task_description: Enabled and optimized real-time synchronization for the shopping cart (cart_items table) across multiple browser tabs and devices. Added cart_items table to the supabase_realtime publication via SQL migration. Refactored CartContext.tsx to incorporate useLeaderElection and BroadcastChannel('ikcous_cart_sync'). Implemented checks to prevent cyclic state updates if remote cart matches local cart exactly.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing real-time syncing for database tables containing user-specific mutable state (such as cart_items), filter the Supabase subscription channel to the logged-in user ID (user_id=eq.${userId}) and structure update flows such that local state changes are skipped if the incoming DB payload is structurally equivalent to local state. This prevents update loop feedback.

entries.task_description: Expanded Leader Election and BroadcastChannel system to coordinate real-time database synchronization for user orders (useOrders.ts), admin layout badges (AdminLayout.tsx), and customer favorites (FavoritesContext.tsx). Created and applied database migration to enable realtime on the favorites table. Safely type-annotated status and err parameters inside subscribe functions to prevent typescript build failures.
entries.lessons_learned: Coordinating general real-time metrics (like layout pending counts) and customer-specific state (like favorites) with Leader Election + BroadcastChannels prevents redundant network requests and socket drops. Ensure explicit types are used inside channel.subscribe callbacks to maintain strict mode compatibility.

entries.task_description: Integrated shipping carrier API quotation (Melhor Envio and Frenet) into the Storefront cart and checkout. Created the reusable premium ShippingCalculator.tsx component with automatic CEP formatting, active loaders, local caching, and offline-first fallback. Integrated the calculator in CartView.tsx, and updated CartContext.tsx to store the chosen option and compute the dynamic shipping fee. Enhanced CheckoutView.tsx to pre-fill the customer's ZIP code from localStorage, keep the guest CEP input fully editable, and append the chosen shipping carrier details (service name and deadline) into the order's internal notes so it is displayed to the store administrator.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing shipping calculation APIs, save the last validated CEP in localStorage and pre-fill the Checkout CEP field to minimize keystrokes and reduce bounce rates. For legacy database schemas without explicit shipping carrier columns, embedding the selected shipping method and delivery days inside the order's observations notes ensures the merchant sees the selection without needing structural schema updates.

entries.task_description: Adjusted the storefront cart's Free Shipping Target (Meta Frete Grátis) to be restricted only to logged-in/authenticated users. When logged out, the progress bar and standard threshold calculations are hidden, and a premium call-to-action (CTA) login banner is displayed to improve conversion. Updated CartContext.tsx to only evaluate freeShippingMin if the user is authenticated, ensuring standard shipping fee calculations are preserved for guests.
entries.lessons_learned: Restricting promotional limits (such as value threshold free shipping) to logged-in states encourages login and signup conversion. Providing visually premium login CTA cards in key transaction hotspots (like the cart view) rather than simply hiding elements creates a better user experience and increases user engagement.

entries.task_description: Consolidated and optimized the storefront cart view layout for guest/logged-out users. Replaced the duplicate free shipping target banner and the redundant checkout options card with a single, unified premium 'Opções de Compra' card positioned below the shipping calculator. Restored ShippingProgress.tsx to its original simple state and restricted its rendering to authenticated users only.
entries.lessons_learned: Avoid rendering multiple high-priority dark theme call-to-action blocks that compete for the same user decision (e.g. logging in) on the same screen. Consolidating login incentives and alternative checkout options (like guest checkout) into a single, structured benefits card simplifies the layout, saves vertical screen space, and guides users with a clear hierarchy.

entries.task_description: Improved the Admin Push Center URL redirect input field. Replaced the manual text input with a high-fidelity, premium Select dropdown containing predefined app destinations (Página Inicial, Busca, Carrinho, Favoritos, Pedidos, Perfil), an optional manual route field, and a dynamic database-connected product selector mapping chosen items directly to product detail routes (/product-detail?id=<id>). Synchronized the selected dropdown option with campaign template loaders and history triggers via a loop-free reactive useEffect.
entries.errors_encountered: Biome organizing imports lint error; resolved automatically via biome check --write --unsafe.
entries.lessons_learned: When replacing text inputs with structured selection dropdowns (Select), synchronize changes bidirecionally with parent values (e.g. templates or URLs) using side-effects (useEffect) with state-guarded conditionals to prevent infinite updates. Querying relational databases (like public.produtos) directly on mount allows quick selections of products without hardcoded strings.

entries.task_description: Optimized storefront visual fluidity, transition smoothness, and component re-render performance. First, implemented custom GPU-accelerated keyframe animation heart-pulse and applied it to the favorites Heart icon in ProductCard and ProductView when active, providing organic and springy visual feedback. Second, memoized high-frequency list and visual indicator components (CartItemsList, OrderList, StarRating) using React.memo to completely bypass virtual DOM reconciliation loops when layout context changes. Third, replaced computationally expensive Framer Motion spring physics with lightweight GPU-driven cubic-bezier easing tweens in ProductList card mounting. Verified with 100% success on fast quality suite checks.
entries.lessons_learned: To prevent layout shifts and maintain 60 FPS scrolling on mobile, heavy spring physics in paginated layouts (like ProductList) should be replaced with cubic-bezier eased GPU-accelerated transforms. Also, wrapping list containers and nested SVGs (like StarRating and CartItemsList) in React.memo reduces CPU overhead dramatically during high-level state updates.

entries.task_description: Performed a production build and deployed the application to Vercel. Verified build logic and syntax integrity through the local quality suite (TypeScript Typecheck, Oxlint, Biome, a11y, Prettier, HTMLHint). Executed a local production build test (`npm run build`) to ensure bundle generation and PWA injectManifest service-worker injection works flawlessly. Initiated production deploy using `npx vercel --prod --yes` which compiled and successfully deployed the frontend live to Vercel.
entries.errors_encountered: Vercel MCP deploy_to_vercel failed with a 'Project name cannot contain sequences of ---' error due to CLI scope detection issues; resolved by running standard npm build and npx vercel CLI deploy directly.
entries.lessons_learned: When Vercel MCP automated command fails with project naming error validation checks, running standard vercel deploy commands directly on the CLI via run_command handles credentials and scope detection correctly by pointing to existing local configurations. Conducting local builds beforehand is essential to guarantee compilation success in the remote cloud environment.

entries.task_description: Resolved a critical production deployment issue where the storefront requested an incorrect/old Supabase project URL and failed to fetch database tables. Fixed a corrupted base64 character ('<' instead of '8') in the VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY inside `.env.production`. Updated the production environment variables VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY on the Vercel Dashboard to point to the correct Core Supabase project (`cafkrminfnokvgjqtkle`). Executed a new production deploy (`npx vercel --prod --yes`) which compiled and successfully deployed the working storefront live.
entries.lessons_learned: Vercel remote builds inject Environment Variables defined on the Vercel Dashboard which override local `.env` files. When changing target databases, ensure variables are synchronized on the Vercel Dashboard project settings and verify that base64 keys are not corrupted by regex or replacement operations.

entries.task_description: Resolved a critical loop reload bug where the storefront continuously refreshed with `?forceUpdate=...`. Identified the root cause as a version mismatch between the database (`min_app_version = '1.0.1'`) and the package.json (`version = '1.0.0'`). Fixed the database value back to `'1.0.0'` and implemented a robust `sessionStorage`-based reload loop guard in `useUpdateCheck.ts` to block infinite refresh loops. Deployed the updated PWA code to Vercel production.
entries.lessons_learned: When implementing auto-updating PWAs based on version checks against a remote database config, always enforce a client-side reload limit (using sessionStorage/localStorage timestamps) to block infinite redirect/reload loops in case of configuration mismatches.
